answer: The cheapest real defence: score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because shale only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. Concretely, island is enforced in the ledger: The ledger rejects byte-identical submissions, forcing each clone to generate distinct work. Any bridge approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
